## Summary

Closed the round-4 alias bypass on the interactive-session write gate (`ai-os/OWNER_DIRECTIVES/interactive-session-guard.bashrc-snippet`):

- **One-shot aliases** (`git -c alias.wip=push wip origin master`) are now rejected outright.
- **Persistent aliases** (a `[alias]` entry in `~/.gitconfig`, or `gh alias set`) are resolved one level via the real `git config --get-regexp '^alias\.'` / `gh alias list`, then evaluated as what they actually expand to.
- Both bypasses were live-reproduced against real git 2.43 / gh 2.45 before the fix, and confirmed blocked after.
- Added 15 new regression scenarios; full suite is **82/82 PASS, exit 0**.
- Honestly disclosed 3 residual gaps found while building this (one-level-only resolution, gh shell aliases, quote-spliced alias values) — each has its own regression test proving the disclosed behavior rather than overclaiming coverage.

**Important complication:** mid-task, PR #80 merged into `master` (commit `ec95532`) carrying the *unpatched* round-4 code — the alias bypass briefly went live in `master`. Since a merged PR can't carry new commits through review, I opened a new PR rather than reusing #80 (per the task's own precedent from round 1), and did **not** merge it myself:

**https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/98**

That PR is open and pending real review/merge through the pipeline.
